structure: Part 3 read the repo-root fit suite in full: fit/live-animals-journey.js (1895 lines, the shared driver every live-animals fit spec imports: sign-in re-export, accessibility, overflow, GOV.UK style and layout helpers, error summary and Back link helpers, the date picker and search box helpers, URL and journey id helpers, the journey form and declaration post, notification view helpers, the happy-path fixture and arrival date, one answer helper per journey page, the LANDINGS table of the ten pages Save and continue lands on, the task-row walk completeAnswerSections, review, submit, amend, cancel-amend, delete and no-JavaScript helpers, and the three save-control shape checks), fit/journey-smoke.fit.spec.js (355 lines, ten tests on the journey glue: Save and continue through the entry guard, one pass to the draft view, Back then Save and continue, three Back-target tests, the incomplete review, the stranger session, Back in reverse to Overview, and collection changes on the review trail), fit/sign-in.js (stub sign-in), playwright.config.js (journeys and features projects, timeouts, stub-mode web server), and the three cross-page feature specs section-caption.fit.spec.js (five tests), page-title.fit.spec.js (two tests) and service-navigation.fit.spec.js (seven tests). It covers the happy path's pages, fields, values and buttons in order, sign-in, what the smoke spec asserts and where it stops (the draft notification view), the caption, title and navigation rules with their exemption and their untested pages, and the suite's own set-up. Since the earlier extract the contact address page has gone from the driver and the smoke spec: consignment addresses now leads straight to the notification view, and the accessibility check gained a second false-positive filter for the GOV.UK file upload button. Each page's own copy belongs to the feature parts.

claims.statement: The live-animals journey is mounted under the path /live-animals, and every notification page sits under /live-animals/notifications/<notification id>.
claims.quote:
export const journeyUrl = (page, slug = '') =>
  `${BASE}/notifications/${journeyIdFromPage(page)}${slug ? `/${slug}` : ''}`

claims.statement: A journey page's URL may carry a from= query holding the trail of pages the trader came through, and the page is the same page with or without it.
claims.quote:
export const urlUnderBase = (pathPattern) =>
  new RegExp(`^https?://[^/]+${BASE}${pathPattern}(?:[?&]from=[^#]*)?$`)

claims.statement: A trader signs in before the journey starts by opening /auth/stub-sign-in with an organisationId, which signs them in as that organisation with no Defra ID stub involved; the fit suite's default organisation is stub-org-1.
claims.note: The route's doc comment says it is "only reachable when STUB_MODE=true".

claims.statement: A test that needs a transporter store no other test shares signs in as a fresh organisation whose id is fit- followed by a random UUID, so the transporter it adds is the newest in that organisation's own store.
claims.quote:
export const signInWithOwnTransporterStore = (page) =>
  signIn(page, { organisationId: `fit-${randomUUID()}` })
claims.note: mechanism: isolates a test's transporter list by organisation id; it works on the transporter store the service keeps per organisation.

claims.statement: The fit suite runs the service by itself in stub mode on PORT (3000 unless set), serving stub data and skipping the Defra ID OIDC exchange, so no other service needs to be running; authorisation is still enforced.
The suite waits for the service's /health endpoint to answer before it runs any test, and starts a fresh server for each run rather than reusing one already listening.
claims.quote:
command: 'npm run fit:start',
      url: `http://localhost:${port}/health`,

claims.statement: The suite runs two projects against the same base URL http://localhost:<port> in Desktop Chrome: a journeys project holding only the journey smoke spec, and a features project holding every *.fit.spec.js under the live-animals features folder.
claims.quote:
name: 'journeys',
      testMatch: '**/journey-smoke.fit.spec.js',

claims.statement: The journeys project records a video and a trace of every run and slows each action by 600 milliseconds so the recorded journey is watchable, which DEMO_SLOWMO overrides; the features project records no video and keeps a trace only when a test fails.
claims.quote:
slowMo:
            process.env.DEMO_SLOWMO !== undefined
              ? Number(process.env.DEMO_SLOWMO)
              : 600

claims.statement: Fit journeys run fully in parallel because each owns its own notification and the store is synchronous, with a 240 second test timeout, a 15 second expectation and action timeout, a 30 second navigation timeout and a screenshot kept only on failure.

The suite seeds no notification data before a journey: each test signs in and then creates its own notification from the set dashboard, so the only data it starts from is the stub reference data and stub address book the service serves in stub mode.
claims.note: It follows because the config declares no globalSetup and no seeding step, and every driver entry point begins at the dashboard's start button.

claims.statement: The set dashboard at /live-animals offers a Start a new notification button, and pressing it creates a notification and opens its origin page at /live-animals/notifications/<id>/origin.
claims.quote:
await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Start a new notification' }).click()
  await expect(page).toHaveURL(urlUnderBase('/notifications/[^/]+/origin'))

claims.statement: A country, port or transit country is chosen through one field that is an enhanced search box when JavaScript runs and a native select when it does not: with JavaScript the trader types a query and picks the named option, without it the option is selected in the select.
claims.quote:
if ((await field.evaluate((el) => el.tagName)) === 'SELECT') {
    await field.selectOption({ label: optionName })
    return
  }
  await field.click()
  await field.fill(query)
  await page.getByRole('option', { name: optionName, exact: true }).click()

Answering Yes on the origin page reveals a region of origin code box labelled "Enter the region of origin code", and the page also takes an optional box labelled "Your internal reference for this consignment (optional)".
claims.quote:
await page.getByRole('radio', { name: 'Yes' }).check()
  await page
    .getByLabel('Enter the region of origin code', { exact: true })
    .fill(regionCode)
  await page
    .getByLabel('Your internal reference for this consignment (optional)')
    .fill(internalReference)

claims.quote:
"countryOfOrigin": "FR",
    "regionOfOriginCodeRequirement": "yes",
    "regionOfOriginCode": "FR-75",
    "internalReferenceNumber": "Imports456GB",
claims.note: The fixture is the repo's own happy-path test data, not a field specification: V4 settles what the origin page captures.

claims.statement: The origin country field is a select with the id countryOfOrigin-select, so a country the reference list does not offer can only reach the page by adding an option to that select.

export const chooseOutOfListCountry = (page, code = 'XX') =>

    .locator('select#countryOfOrigin-select')
claims.note: mechanism: appends an option to the origin country select so a test can post a code the list does not hold; it works on the country reference list the page renders.

claims.statement: On the commodities search page a species is found by typing its Latin name into the search box and pressing a Search button, then ticking that species' checkbox inside the group named by its commodity code.

    await expect(

claims.quote: Starts a notification, answers origin and opens the import reason page by address, leaving commodities unanswered.

return page

name:

claims.statement: Saving the animal identification page with no animal identified still opens the additional details page, so identifying an animal is not needed to carry on.

The additional details page asks what the animals are certified for, the happy path choosing Slaughter, and asks "Does the consignment contain any unweaned animals?" as its own group, answered No; saving opens the arrival details page.
Leaving the certified-for or unweaned question unanswered and leaving the additional details page by Save and return to overview takes the trader to the overview rather than refusing the page.

The arrival details page, at the slug port-of-entry and headed "Arrival details", asks for the arrival date at the port of entry, the port of entry, the means of transport, a transport identification and a transport document reference.
claims.quote:
await page
    .getByLabel('Arrival date at port of entry')
    .fill(ARRIVAL_DATE_IN_WINDOW)
  await choosePortOfEntry(page)
  await chooseMeansOfTransport(page, values.meansOfTransport)

claims.statement: The arrival date the happy path enters is one month after today, so the date always falls inside the window the page accepts.
claims.quote:
const arrivalDate = addUtcMonths(new Date(), 1)
export const ARRIVAL_DATE_IN_WINDOW = formatDateText(arrivalDate)
claims.note: mechanism: computes a date inside the arrival window rather than using the fixture's fixed 12/12/2026; it works on the arrival date the page validates.

claims.statement: An arrival date is shown back to the trader as the day, the three-letter month and the year, such as "3 Mar 2026", while it is typed into the arrival details page in the date text format the calendar helper writes.
claims.quote: return `${date.getUTCDate()} ${shortMonths[date.getUTCMonth()]} ${date.getUTCFullYear()}`
claims.note: The driver exports ARRIVAL_DATE_IN_WINDOW_DISPLAY for specs that read the date back; where it is shown is the feature parts' claim.

A transporter chosen on the list and saved stays chosen: reopening the transporters page shows that transporter's radio checked.

The transporter list has an Add a transporter button that opens a type question, "Choose a transporter type", whose Commercial and Private options each lead, through the question's own Continue button, to that type's own add page.
After a transporter is added the transporter list is shown again under a success banner naming the transporter that was added.

claims.statement: Once every party and the CPH number are added, Save and continue on the consignment addresses page opens the notification view, which shows the notification as a draft; no contact address page comes between them.
claims.quote:
await addPlaceOfDestination(page)
  await answerCphNumberFromAddLink(page)
  await save(page)
  await expectDraftReview(page)
claims.note: The driver holds no contact address step anywhere: no landing, no helper and no task row for one.

claims.statement: An address in a party picker is shown by the name on the record, and a party answered from the address book shows the name that book record carries.
claims.quote:
export const partyPickerName = (party) =>
  party?.name ?? stubNameById.get(party?.addressId)
claims.note: mechanism: resolves a fixture party to the name its picker row shows, by the record's own name or by looking its address id up in the stub book.

claims.statement: The notification overview is the notification's root page, headed "Overview", and each part of the notification is opened from it by a link reading that task row's title.

The whole notification can be answered one overview task row at a time, in the order: Where is this consignment coming from?, What are you importing?, Commodity details, Identification details, Main import reason, Additional details, Consignment addresses, Arrival details, Transit countries, Transport details; Transport details is the last row the walk answers.
claims.quote:
await task('Arrival details')
  await answerArrivalDetails(page)
  await openOverview(page)
  if (!skipTransitCountries) {
    await task('Transit countries')
    await answerTransitCountries(page)
    await openOverview(page)
  }
  await task('Transport details')
  await answerTransporter(page)
  await openOverview(page)
}
claims.note: This order is the driver's own walk of the task rows, and it differs from the Save and continue order, where the main import reason comes before the commodity details. The walk leaves the Upload documents row unanswered; a document is added only when a test asks for one.

claims.statement: A notification is opened for review by a "Review and submit" button on the overview, which opens the notification view at the slug notification-view.
claims.quote:
await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Review and submit' }).click()
  await expect(page).toHaveURL(
    urlUnderBase('/notifications/[^/]+/notification-view')

claims.statement: A draft notification's view is headed by the notification's own reference, shows the status Draft and ends with one control only, the review's submit button.

A complete notification is submitted from the notification view by pressing Continue, ticking a declaration checkbox that begins "I confirm that I have reviewed", then pressing Continue again, and the notification keeps the same reference through the submission.
claims.quote:
await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Continue' }).click()
  await page
    .getByRole('checkbox', { name: /I confirm that I have reviewed/ })
    .check()
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Continue' }).click()
  return journeyIdFromPage(page)

An amendment changes an answer through a Change link on the notification view, such as "Change origin of import", which opens the question page; saving it carries on to the next journey page.
claims.quote: await page.getByRole('link', { name: 'Change origin of import' }).click()

claims.statement: A notification is deleted from its view by a Delete control among the notification actions, which opens a confirmation page with its own level 1 heading rather than a pop-up.
Each journey page's answers are posted by one form whose method is post, and the page's save controls sit inside it.
claims.quote: export const JOURNEY_FORM_SELECTOR = 'form[method="post"]'

claims.statement: A journey page's form carries a concurrency token alongside its answers, which is posted back as the page rendered it.
claims.quote:
Every other field the form
 * holds, the concurrency token included, is sent as the page rendered it.
claims.note: mechanism: reposts a page's own form to another path with chosen fields replaced; it works on the hidden fields the journey form renders.

claims.statement: A notification's declaration is posted to /live-animals/notifications/<id>/declaration from the journey form, carrying the form's own fields as the page rendered them.

const declarationPath = new URL(journeyUrl(page, 'declaration'), page.url())
    .pathname
claims.note: mechanism: a driver helper that reposts a page's form to the declaration path; the route's existence is read from the path the helper targets.

claims.note: The shared copy reads 'Save and continue', 'Save and return to overview' and 'Cancel and return to overview'. Which pages show all three is each feature part's claim; this is the shape the driver holds a page to.

claims.statement: A page must have no serious or critical accessibility violation against WCAG 2.0 A and AA, WCAG 2.1 A and AA and WCAG 2.2 AA.
claims.quote: .withTags(['wcag2a', 'wcag2aa', 'wcag21a', 'wcag21aa', 'wcag22aa'])

claims.statement: The accessibility check ignores, as a false positive, an aria-allowed-attr violation reported only against GOV.UK radio or checkbox inputs, which is how the GOV.UK conditional reveal is built.
claims.quote:
const isGovukConditionalRevealFalsePositive = (violation) =>
  violation.id === 'aria-allowed-attr' &&
  violation.nodes.every((node) =>
    /govuk-(radios|checkboxes)__input/.test(node.html)
  )

claims.statement: The accessibility check also ignores, as a false positive, a label-content-name-mismatch violation reported only against the GOV.UK file upload button.
claims.quote:
const isGovukFileUploadFalsePositive = (violation) =>
  violation.id === 'label-content-name-mismatch' &&
  violation.nodes.every((node) =>
    /class="govuk-file-upload-button[ "]/.test(node.html)
  )

claims.statement: Back steps through the pages Save and continue visited in reverse order and then ends on the Overview at the notification's root address.

claims.statement: The section caption spec proves the caption on only three pages, the origin page, the main import reason page and the dashboard, and names no caption for the other sections the set declares, so nothing holds the remaining pages to the rule.
claims.note: Looked at every test in the file: five tests, covering origin, import reason, the dashboard, the overview exemption and the axe check. The section-captions copy names nine sections (dashboard, about the consignment, description of the goods, commodity details, addresses, movement, transport and arrival, add a new transporter, documents); seven of them have no test here.

claims.statement: A page's browser title reads the page's own name, then the service name, then GOV.UK, joined by spaced hyphens: "<page name> - Import notification service - GOV.UK".
When a page is showing errors its title gets the prefix "Error: " in front of the whole title, the page name, service name and GOV.UK included.
Answering Yes on the origin page's region question and saving with no region of origin code shows the error "Enter the region of origin code" as a link in the error summary.
The page title rule is proven on the origin page alone, both plain and with an error, so no other page in the set is held to the title pattern.
claims.note: Looked at both tests in the file: each signs in and opens the origin page in beforeEach, and neither visits another page.
